# A Julia Figure

The cell below renders a Plots.jl figure as a PNG **file** (not an inline
base64 data-URI). Three things make that happen:

1. `ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"` (set before `using Plots`) forces GR's GKS
   backend to the headless cairo-PNG workstation, so no interactive `gksqt`
   Qt workstation is spawned. In a windowed macOS session GR would otherwise
   default to `gksqt`, which blocks the notebook worker.
2. `savefig(p, path)` renders the plot to a PNG file through that headless
   workstation.
3. The cell returns a `PngFigure` wrapper that is showable **only** as
   `image/png` (no `text/html` show method). QuartoNotebookRunner captures
   only the `image/png` MIME; q2's `displayDataMimeType` then selects
   `image/png` (a default Plots plot is `text/html`-showable and would be
   emitted inline instead — see the 4CD MIME finding), and the jupyter
   `toMarkdown` image branch (`mdImageOutput`) writes the figure to
   `plot_files/figure-html/*.png` and references it via `<img src=...>`.

```{julia}
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using Plots
p = plot(1:10, rand(10))
path = tempname() * ".png"
savefig(p, path)

struct PngFigure
    bytes::Vector{UInt8}
end
Base.show(io::IO, ::MIME"image/png", f::PngFigure) = write(io, f.bytes)

PngFigure(read(path))
```
